name: E-Commerce Defective Smartphone Refund Denial
raw_input: I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on an e-commerce app on 10th November 2024. It was delivered on 14th November. Within 24 hours of opening the box, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working. I raised a replacement request on 15th November. The app sent a technician for inspection on 21st November. The technician confirmed it is a manufacturing hardware defect and took sign on his job sheet. But on 23rd November, customer support cancelled my return request stating 'The 7-day return window expired on 21st November'. They are telling me to go to an authorized brand service center 40 km away. I paid for a brand new working phone, not a defective phone repaired on day one. I have the invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots.

case_dossier.case_title: Defective Smartphone Delivery and Wrongful Replacement Denial
case_dossier.summary: The complainant ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 which arrived with a manufacturing defect. Although a technician inspected and confirmed the defect within the return period, customer support cancelled the replacement request citing the expiry of the 7-day return window and asked the user to visit a distant service center.

timeline.event: Ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone on the e-commerce app.
Smartphone was delivered to the complainant.
Screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working.
Raised a replacement request on the e-commerce app.
Technician inspected the device, confirmed manufacturing hardware defect, and took signature on job sheet.
Customer support cancelled the return request stating the 7-day return window expired on 21st November.

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
Your complaint regarding a defective smartphone and the seller's unfair denial of replacement is fully protected under consumer law.
Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, delivering faulty goods and refusing to refund or replace them constitutes a statutory deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.
You have the right to seek a complete replacement or refund along with compensation for the trouble caused, and you can represent yourself without needing a lawyer in the Consumer Commission.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects you as a consumer who bought goods for a consideration.
Defines a defect in goods covering faults or imperfections in quality and standards.
Defines deficiency in service covering negligence or omission in fulfilling a contract.
Qualifies refusing to refund or replace defective goods within stipulated terms as an unfair trade practice.
Provides the procedure for filing a consumer complaint electronically or physically.

action_options.title: Lodge Preliminary Grievance and Serve Notice
action_options.details: Lodge a formal grievance on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) via toll-free number 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in. Simultaneously, serve a formal 15-day legal demand notice to the seller and e-commerce platform attaching your invoice and technician job sheet.

action_options.title: File Electronic Complaint on e-Jagriti Portal
action_options.details: File an electronic consumer complaint online on e-Jagriti (launched 1 Jan 2025, replacing e-Daakhil). Upload your order invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots. Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance (Helpline 15100) only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings.

action_options.title: Proceed with District Consumer Commission Petition
action_options.details: If the seller fails to resolve the issue after the notice and online grievance, pursue your formal petition before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for product replacement, refund, and compensation.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can represent yourself entirely on your own before the Consumer Commission without hiring a physical advocate, as the Consumer Protection Act allows consumers to argue their own cases.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
### LEGAL NOTICE DRAFT – REVIEW BEFORE SENDING

**FROM:** 
[Your Name] 
[Your Address] 
Phone: [Your Phone Number] 
Email: [Your Email Address] 

**DATE:** 09/11/2026 

**MODE OF DISPATCH:** Speed Post (Acknowledgment Due) / Registered Email 

**TO:** 
The E-commerce Platform / Seller Management 
[Recipient Company Name / Seller Name] 
[Recipient Address] 
[Recipient Email Address] 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR REPLACEMENT/REFUND OF DEFECTIVE SMARTPHONE AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE UNDER THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019.**

Dear Sir/Madam,

I, am serving this legal demand notice upon you in my individual capacity as a consumer, setting forth my grievance regarding the delivery of a defective smartphone and the subsequent arbitrary cancellation of my replacement request.

I hereby state and submit as under:

1. That on 10th November 2024, I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on your e-commerce app, bearing Order ID [Insert Order ID / Details]. I paid the full consideration amount of Rs 26,999 for the purchase, confirming my status as a consumer under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

2. That the said smartphone was delivered to me on 14th November 2024 along with the invoice and delivery receipt. 

3. That within 24 hours of delivery, serious hardware defects manifested in the device: the screen started flickering with green lines and the touch functionality stopped working entirely.

4. That immediately upon noticing the defect, on 15th November 2024, I raised a formal replacement request on your e-commerce app within the stipulated return window.

5. That on 21st November 2024, an authorized technician visited to inspect the device, confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and took my signature on the job sheet. 

6. That despite the technician's confirmation well within time, on 23rd November 2024, your customer support arbitrarily cancelled my return request, stating that the 7-day return window expired on 21st November 2024, and advised me to visit a distant service center. This cancellation disregards the fact that my replacement request and inspection were initiated and processed within the applicable timelines.

7. That delivering a defective product and subsequently refusing to provide a replacement or refund—despite timely reporting and technician verification—constitutes a clear "defect" in goods under Section 2(10), "deficiency in service" under Section 2(11), and an "unfair trade practice" under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

8. That I am holding the following evidentiary documents in support of my claim:
 - Invoice
 - Delivery receipt
 - Technician inspection job sheet copy
 - Chat screenshots

**DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION:**

In light of the above facts and statutory provisions, I hereby call upon you to rectify this grievance within a suggested 15-day period (customary pre-litigation practice) from the receipt of this notice, by taking the following actions:

1. Arrange for an immediate pickup and complete replacement of the defective Samsung Galaxy smartphone with a brand-new, unblemished unit, OR alternatively, process a full refund of Rs 26,999 to my original payment source.
2. Pay reasonable compensation for the mental agony, physical inconvenience, and deficiency in service caused by your arbitrary refusal.

**WARNING:**

Please take notice that if you fail to comply with the demands made above within the suggested 15-day period, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal proceedings against you by filing a consumer complaint electronically on the e-Jagriti Portal or before the competent District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, seeking product replacement, full refund, costs, and compensation, at your sole risk, cost, and consequences.

For guidance or free legal aid inquiries prior to filing, the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline is available at 15100.

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name] 

---

**ANNEXURE INVENTORY:**
1. Copy of Order Invoice
2. Copy of Delivery Receipt
3. Copy of Technician Inspection Job Sheet
4. Copies of Chat Screenshots with Customer Support

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under Section 2(11) and Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, delivering a defective phone and delaying inspection past your return window is a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. I have the technician report confirming hardware fault. I demand an immediate refund or I will escalate to the National Consumer Helpline and e-Jagriti.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre sir, why are you shouting Consumer Protection Act and all? Look, system is system! Return window is 7 days only, policy is policy. Technician report is fine, but company approval needs time. If you want, go to service center and get it repaired. Refund is not possible now.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You clearly cited specific sections of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(11) for deficiency in service and Section 84 for product liability/unfair trade practices) along with concrete proof (the technician report).
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Keep holding your ground on the exact date the technician inspected the phone within the 7-day window. Emphasize that their internal system delay cannot override statutory rights.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Your internal return window cannot override statutory rights under the Consumer Protection Act when the defect and technician verification happened well within the 7 days.
